## Negative result independently confirmed — and better explained

The coordinator corroborated the finding above and supplied the missing half of the
explanation for the one signal I had classified as nondeterministic.

`test_terraform_code_review_tools.py::test_ac3_verifier_routing_gets_distinct_fresh_terraform_session`
(`assert (2 >= 2 and 1 == 2)`) was **an already-fixed defect**, closed under
`naval-halfasleep-shorebird` and landed as change 2669. The three scheduled runs I compared
(33967035958 / 33956014400 / 33950878570) **straddle that fix** rather than being three
executions of one tree — which is why it failed in two and passed in the third. So it was
never a flake at all: it is a deterministic defect observed on both sides of its own repair,
and the pass/fail split is explained by the head sha, not by nondeterminism.

That leaves the record cleaner than my earlier comment stated. Corrected reading of today's
three scheduled `main` failures:

- **None** share this ticket's detached-maintenance mechanism. Unchanged.
- The gating-cell signal is **not** an outstanding second main-red producer — it is fixed,
  and no dispatch is needed. My earlier note recommending someone be dispatched at it is
  superseded by this.
- The sweep-tier failures (`test_reconcile_once_threads_composed_runtime_transport_into_apply`
  on macos/py3.14t/py3.15, and the Windows platform set) remain deterministic and unrelated.

This also settles severity for good. There is no longer any candidate reading under which this
bug explains `main`'s recent noise, so **p2 stands** — it is a real ADR-0051 invariant hole
worth closing on its own merits, with exactly two observed instances (the 2682 pytest failure
and the `test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py` `git clone … exit 128` in run 33970977028), and
nothing beyond that. Recorded so a future reader does not re-derive a bigger claim from the
same evidence.
